finding: The diff adds `- 'sdk'` to the pull_request path filter so 'a kit regression arrives as a gitlink bump' fires this job — but the job's checkout (line 40, `actions/checkout@v4`) has NO `submodules: recursive`, unlike hub-smoke.yml:52, server-release.yml:37 and desktop-release.yml:38 which all set it. The kit under test lives at `sdk/packages/kit`, which the root package.json declares as an npm workspace (`sdk/packages/*`) that `src-app/ui/package.json`'s `"@ziee/kit": "*"` resolves to. With the submodule uncheckedd out, `sdk/` is an empty dir: `npm ci` cannot resolve the workspace link, and the new `input-group-overflow.spec.ts` can never exercise the changed kit. The one new CI trigger the diff adds is therefore inert (at best it runs against a kit that is not the one in the gitlink), so the stated remedy for 'the exact change class that broke (and fixed) the InputGroup addon' is unproven. Add `with: submodules: recursive` (and the same to visual-snapshots.yml:43).

The two RTL rows of TEST-7 cannot go red for the defect they are credited with. The removed rules were PHYSICAL (`has-[>button]:mr-[-0.3rem]` on inline-end, `ml-[-0.3rem]` on inline-start — sdk2.diff:58,61). Under RTL the `order-last` inline-end addon is the LEFTMOST flex item, so its `margin-right` faces the group's INTERIOR and a negative value pulls the input inward; symmetrically the `order-first` inline-start addon is rightmost and its `margin-left` faces inward. The pre-fix kit therefore produced ZERO overhang and ZERO `scrollWidth-clientWidth` in RTL — both RTL cases were green before the fix and are green after it. The header (line 12-16) claims RTL is included 'because the fix's whole rationale was replacing physical margins with logical padding, and only an RTL render can show whether that actually holds', but an overflow/containment probe is exactly the measurement a physical-vs-logical swap does NOT move; what would move is the addon's INSET symmetry, which the spec computes as `addonPastEdge` yet only tests as `> JITTER_PX`. The falsifiability control (line 190) is LTR-only, so nothing demonstrates the RTL rows can fail at all.

Three of the four changed addon utilities have no assertion that can go red. Grepping the tree: the ONLY `InputGroupAddon` with a direct `> button` child is combobox.tsx:79 (`align="inline-end"`); command.tsx:82 uses the default inline-start with an `svg` child; `grep -rn InputGroupAddon src-app/ui/src src-app/desktop/ui/src` returns NOTHING (no app usage); and no gallery story renders a `kbd` addon. So `inline-start: ps-2 has-[>button]:ps-1 has-[>kbd]:ps-1.5` and `inline-end: has-[>kbd]:pe-1.5` are changed with no rendered instance. The anti-vacuity guard at line 163 counts `hasButtonChild` across BOTH aligns, so the single inline-end combobox satisfies it while the file header (line 12-14) explicitly credits the spec with covering 'BOTH inline-start and inline-end addons ... a guard on one of them lets the other rot'. The guard should be per-align (and a kbd story added) or the claim dropped.

No test — unit, integration, or E2E — ever RUNS a workflow step whose wording comes from a `prompt_file:`. `grep -rn prompt_file src-app/server/tests/` returns only builder_validate_def_test.rs (a /validate-def payload; that endpoint has no bundle so it never reads a file). The new tests drive `load_raw_prompt` directly with an explicit `root`, so the two production wirings that supply that root — `resolve_prompt` at dispatch.rs:92 (used by LlmDispatcher:182 and agent_dispatch.rs:1099) and `load_raw_prompt(&step.id, &ctx.extracted_path, ...)` at dispatch.rs:393 (llm_map) — are untested. Replacing `ctx.extracted_path` with any other path (workspace dir, run dir) turns NO test red, yet that is the whole reason the signature was narrowed from `&RunContext` to `(&str, &Path)`. The originally-reported symptom ('validated clean, then failed the RUN' — FIX_ROUND-8) is likewise never reproduced end-to-end. Also uncovered: a prompt_file whose body contains `{{ }}` templates through `resolve_prompt`'s render step.

`client_prompt_file_predicate_mirrors_prompt_source` never EXECUTES the TypeScript — it substring-scans the extracted function body and asserts only (a) it contains one of `length > 0` / `!== ''` / `length !== 0` and (b) it does not contain `.trim()`. An exact logical INVERSION, `return !(typeof pf === 'string' && pf.length > 0)`, passes both assertions; so does `pf.length > 0 || pf === 'x'`, or a body that flips the `typeof` guard (which is not asserted at all). The name and the doc claim the predicate 'mirrors `prompt_source`' EXACTLY and that the guard 'fails the BACKEND suite if these two drift' (stepForms.ts:1331-1333 repeats the promise). It does catch the one specific regression (dropping `pf.length > 0`), but the guarantee credited to it is far wider than the assertion. A value-level mirror (a tiny node one-liner, or a shared JSON table of (prompt, prompt_file) -> verdict asserted from both suites) is what the doc describes.

The control injects a DIFFERENT rule from the one that was removed, contrary to its own documentation. `REVERTED_RULE` is `margin-inline-end:-0.3rem` (LOGICAL); the kit carried `mr-[-0.3rem]` (PHYSICAL `margin-right`) — sdk2.diff:61. Line 43 calls it 'The exact rule that was removed' and line 1568-1570 argues at length that a control injecting a different defect proves nothing. In LTR the two coincide so the LTR control is still valid, but (i) the claim of exactness is false, and (ii) it is precisely why no RTL control exists: in RTL the logical injection WOULD produce overflow while the physical original never did, so an RTL control would go green for a defect that was never shipped. It also injects only 1 of the 4 removed declarations (nothing for `inline-start`, nothing for either `kbd` variant).

The fix's comment states measured spacing values — 'the child's inset from the group's inner edge moves 3.20px -> 4.00px (button) and 5.61px -> 6.00px (kbd) ... and the input-to-child gap is unchanged at 6.00px in LTR' — and the stated rationale is grid alignment (8px bare / 4px button / 6px kbd). NO test asserts any spacing VALUE. `input-group-overflow.spec.ts` computes `addonPastEdge` (line 108) but only ever filters `> JITTER_PX`, i.e. it answers 'is the addon outside the group', never 'is it inset by 4px'. Consequently `pe-1` -> `pe-0`, `pe-1` -> `pe-8`, a return to off-grid arbitrary values, or an addon that collapses to zero width / `display:none` (zero-size rects trivially satisfy both `toEqual([])` assertions while `hasButtonChild` still reads true from the DOM) all stay green. The two 'independent signals' at lines 175/183 are not independent: both are satisfied by any layout where the addon is inside or absent.

`prompt_codes_list_covers_every_prompt_verdict_the_validator_emits` has no production line whose revert turns it red — it compares a test-local constant against a raw text scan of `include_str!("validate.rs")`, and that scan includes validate.rs's own `#[cfg(test)]` module. So deleting a production emit while any test assertion still names the code keeps the guard green: e.g. removing the `PromptFileError::Unsafe` arm would still leave `"WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE"` as a literal in TEST-3 (validate.rs:2011) and in the pre-existing prompt_file_unsafe test. Conversely a quoted code in a doc comment would fail it spuriously. It also scans ONLY validate.rs, so a prompt verdict emitted from any other module is invisible to the guard whose stated job is 'the validator must not gain a prompt-related code that this matrix silently stops covering'. Scan the emit sites structurally (ValidationError::at call arguments) rather than the whole file text.

The author-facing copy for `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING` is rewritten to cover four distinct causes ('missing, be a folder rather than a file, be empty, or not be text'), which is the user-visible half of the semantics change — and nothing asserts it. `validationCopy.test.ts` pins copy for `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_MISSING` (lines 53/68) and `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_BOTH` (line 138) but has no case for `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING`. The only guard that touches it is validate.rs's HUMAN_COPY key-presence drift guard (~line 3294), which passed identically with the OLD copy, so it cannot detect that the remedy text and the code's meaning have diverged again. Given that three of the four causes now share one code, the copy IS the disambiguation and deserves a pinned test.

`check_prompt_files` now calls `read_prompt_file`, i.e. a full synchronous `std::fs::read_to_string` of EVERY `prompt_file:` in the definition, with no size cap, inside `validate_collecting` — which the install/import path calls from async request handling. dispatch.rs:137 deliberately wraps the same call in `spawn_blocking`; the validator side does not. No test covers a large prompt_file, a many-prompt-file bundle, or the added blocking cost, so a bundle carrying a multi-GB `prompt_file:` is an untested resource path on the validation surface that previously only did `canonicalize()`.

The two new distinguished error strings are asserted only at the pure-function level (dispatch.rs:2100 and 2118). Nothing asserts what the OPERATOR sees: `LlmMapDispatcher` wraps them as `StepResult::Failed { error: format!("prompt load: {e}") }` (dispatch.rs:397) and `agent_dispatch.rs:1102` wraps `resolve_prompt`'s error as `agent prompt render: {e}` — so the message a failed run actually surfaces is untested, as is the whole point of the doc's claim that the distinction matters 'exactly when the operator has least context' (dispatch.rs:147-148). Also untested: the `spawn_blocking` JoinError branch at dispatch.rs:141.

'an EMPTY prompt_file leaves the prompt requirement in force' asserts only `prompt_file: ''` (requirement stands) and `prompt_file: 'p.md'` (requirement lifted) through `configErrors`. It never exercises `prompt_file: '   '`, even though the sibling test at line 415 pins `promptSuppliedByFile('   ') === true` as THE load-bearing is_empty()-not-trim() boundary and the Rust drift guard's entire second assertion is about trimming. So the consequence half of the mirror is narrower than the predicate half: a future `configErrors` that trimmed independently of `promptSuppliedByFile` would go undetected here.

The docstring states 'INV-1: a def this endpoint reports clean must run, and one it rejects must not quietly run', but the test only POSTs to /workflows/validate-def and inspects `errors[].code` — it never runs anything, and the endpoint deliberately answers no file-existence question. The assertion is strictly about three validator verdicts; the run half of the implication is credited to this test and delivered by none. (The anti-vacuity controls themselves are sound: the MISSING case at line 172 and the BOTH control at line 194 both show the checks still fire.)

`check_prompt_file_shape` (line 1179) and `prompt_file_ref` (line 1121) are declared `pub` but have no caller outside validate.rs — grep across src/ and tests/ shows only validate.rs:1208/1272 and validate.rs:1105/1267. dispatch.rs imports only `prompt_source`, `PromptSource` and `read_prompt_file`. Not dead code, but the visibility overstates the API surface of a module whose stated design is 'ONE rule both sides go through': a future caller can legitimately reach for the shape-only half and bypass the confinement+read that INV-1 depends on. `pub(crate)` (or private for `prompt_file_ref`) matches the intent.

'rtl' : 'ltr'` in an inline head script before any module loads, so `getComputedStyle(el).direction` is genuinely 'rtl' at first paint.

REJECTED: candidate that the hard-coded `assert_eq!(checked, 108)` is wrong. Verified: 3 kinds (llm, llm_map, agent) x 4 prompts (None, "", "   ", "hi") x 9 files = 108. Adding or removing a row makes this assertion fail loudly rather than silently shrinking the matrix.

REJECTED: candidates that (a) `assert_eq!(ran_ok, 18)` is arithmetically wrong and (b) TEST-1's biconditional is unfalsifiable against changes to the SHARED rule (since both sides now call `prompt_source`/`read_prompt_file`, a lockstep change keeps the implication true). Arithmetic verified: per kind the runnable rows are {None,""} x prompts/real.md = 2 plus {"   ","hi"} x {None,""} = 4, i.e. 6; 6 x 3 = 18. And `ran_ok` is exactly what closes the lockstep hole: dropping the zero-byte check makes empty.md runnable -> 24; dropping `check_prompt_file_shape` makes `prompts/../prompts/real.md` runnable -> 24; trimming in `prompt_source` makes `"   "` absent -> 12. Each turns the test RED.
